name: Basics of Advanced Planning: Methodology and Application in a Business Game Simulation
description:
Today’s business is characterized by supply networks comprising different partners (e.g. suppliers, production plants, distribution and retail centres, and customers). Activities within supply networks have to be well coordinated in order to avoid excessive inventories, inefficient capacity utilization and poor customer service.

In most industrial companies operational production management is supported by computerized production planning and control (PPC) systems. Over the recent years the so-called Advanced Planning and Scheduling (APS) systems have emerged which cover the planning tasks related to PPC systems in a supply chain framework. Their major characteristics are the use of mathematical optimization techniques and the integration of PPC into comprehensive supply chain management concepts.

One key difficulty in managing complex supply chains is that decisions are distributed across multiple organizational units, like purchasing, operations and sales. Decisions made in one unit have an impact on the other units as well, requiring adjustments in their operational decisions. This requires good communication and alignment.

This course applies a blended learning concept. Theoretical concepts for planning problems in supply chain management, PPC and APS are presented in a classroom lecture. The lecture includes in-class practice exercises. In parallel to the in-class lecture, students pair up in teams of 4 to play “The Fresh Connection”, a business game simulation about a fruit juice company. Over the course of the whole semester the students manage the company by making decisions in purchasing, supply chain management, production and sales. The game is played in multiple rounds, with new challenges arising in each round. With simulation students experience the effects of their supply chain decisions first hand. Selected topics of the game and results will be discussed in-class. The best student team per semester gets the chance to participate in a global student challenge, organized by the company behind the game.


Content:
1. Fundamentals of Production Planning and Control Systems
2. Introduction to Supply Chain Management
3. Advanced Planning Systems
5. Demand Planning
6. Supply Network Planning
7. Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling
8. Available-to-Promise and Deployment
9. Transportation Planning
10. Business game simulation “The Fresh Connection”
prerequisites:
It is expected that participants have an interest in practical problems of production planning, scheduling and logistics, and the quantitative modelling of business problems. Participants should be familiar with basic Operations Research (OR) techniques.

The module "Produktionsmanagement" is a prerequisite.

Additionally, the prior participation in the module "Modelling, Optimization and Simulation in Operations Management" is desirable.
